accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 44, printed 30, lines 4-19: introduction, all five convention bullets, ten abbreviation entries, and five metasymbol entries are subdivided below. These define the document's notation, not additional executable Fortran features.

PDF 44 lines 4-5: the modified BNF describes forms of lexical tokens, statements, and constructs. Source-census review, not a running program, is the appropriate evidence for interpreting this notation.

First bullet, PDF 44 lines 6-7: displayed Fortran characters denote themselves unless another interpretation is explicitly specified. The Clause 6 character repertoire remains a dependency; the exception prevents treating every printed bracket as a literal source character.

Second bullet, PDF 44 lines 8-9: lower-case italic terms, including abbreviated and hyphenated terms, are placeholders for members of syntactic classes. The substitution language is a metalanguage rule, not a requirement to write those italic terms literally in Fortran.
PDF 44 after line 10: account for both columns of the five-row abbreviation display. These are common term abbreviations, not an exhaustive grammar or additional keywords.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 1 left: arg denotes argument.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 1 right: attr denotes attribute.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 2 left: decl denotes declaration.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 2 right: def denotes definition.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 3 left: desc denotes descriptor.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 3 right: expr denotes expression.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 4 left: int denotes integer.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 4 right: op denotes operator.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 5 left: spec denotes specifier.
PDF 44, abbreviation display row 5 right: stmt denotes statement.
Third bullet, PDF 44 after line 11: all five display rows are accounted below. The final marker is a filled square, visually checked in the pinned PDF; text extraction omits that glyph.
Display row 1: is starts the definition of a syntactic class; it is not a Fortran token in the represented statement.
Display row 2: or introduces an alternative for the same syntactic class.
Display row 3: metalanguage square brackets indicate optional material, not literal source brackets unless separately specified.
Display row 4: brackets followed by an ellipsis permit zero or more repetitions of the bracketed material. They do not impose a positive repetition count or a processor-independent maximum.
Display row 5: the filled-square marker continues the printed syntax rule. It is unrelated to source-form ampersand or column-six continuation.

Fourth bullet, PDF 44 lines 12-14: R identifiers are unique, with a one- or two-digit clause component and a two-digit within-clause sequence. Rules occur throughout the document and are cross-referenced by these identifiers. This does not require a compiler diagnostic to print a rule code.

Fourth bullet qualification, PDF 44 lines 14-16: some rules introduced in Clauses 5 and 6 use the number of the later clause where they are repeated and more fully specified. A restatement is not a new local rule or independent requirement owner.

Fifth bullet, PDF 44 lines 17-19: the displayed grammar alone is deliberately insufficient for automatically constructing a correct parser. Associated constraints and surrounding text restrict incomplete productions. Grammar extraction cannot establish whole-source coverage or discard normative prose.

PDF 44 note below line 19: a local digit-string illustration, including four schematic forms. Its numerical examples continue on PDF 45, separately inventoried as note-unnumbered.2. This disposition concerns only this note.
The note illustrates one initial digit followed by optional repeated digits; it is not a newly owned normative digit-string rule.
First schematic form illustrates the zero-repetition branch after the initial digit.
Second schematic form illustrates one repetition after the initial digit.
Third schematic form illustrates three repetitions after the initial digit.
Fourth schematic form illustrates seven repetitions after the initial digit; the example is not a maximum length.

PDF 45, printed 31, continued note above line 1: all four concrete examples complete the PDF 44 illustration. Its lexical examples do not promise that every illustrated number fits every default-integer representation.
First concrete example instantiates the one-position schematic form.
Second concrete example instantiates the two-position schematic form.
Third concrete example instantiates the four-position schematic form.
Fourth concrete example instantiates the eight-position schematic form, without imposing a portable integer-kind requirement.
